sources.title: Amazon S3: Uploading objects
sources.version_or_commit: AWS S3 User Guide, live documentation; page version not stated
sources.locator: Upload a single object; Upload an object in parts; Console upload limits
sources.observed_operation: Amazon S3 single PUT/PutObject; multipart upload; separate S3 console upload workflow
sources.claim_scope: The page states a 5 GB limit for a single PUT request, a 160 GB limit for the console workflow, and describes multipart objects from 5 MB to 50 TB.
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: The single-request and console statements govern different operations. Units in the multipart summary differ from the quota page's binary expression. These are AWS S3 statements only.
sources.applicability: Comparison baseline only; archive provider and supported subset are unknown.

sources.title: Amazon S3: Amazon S3 quotas
sources.version_or_commit: AWS S3 User Guide, live documentation; page version not stated
sources.locator: Multipart upload and object size limits
sources.claim_scope: Maximum object size 48.8 TiB; 10,000 parts numbered 1–10,000; part sizes 5 MiB–5 GiB; no minimum size for the final part.
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: AWS quota facts only. ListParts and ListMultipartUploads listing limits are 1,000 per response and require pagination.
sources.applicability: Comparison baseline only; not an archive-provider limit.

sources.title: Amazon S3: Multipart upload overview
sources.version_or_commit: AWS S3 User Guide, live documentation; page version not stated
sources.locator: Multipart upload process; listing parts; completing and aborting multipart uploads
sources.claim_scope: Multipart uploads have an upload ID; reusing a part number replaces that part; completion assembles selected parts in ascending order; multipart ETag is not necessarily MD5 of the object.
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: ListParts is paginated at 1,000 and used for verification, not as the completion manifest. Incomplete uploads do not expire by default; explicitly complete or abort. Stored parts are billed until completion/abort.
sources.applicability: Amazon S3 behavior only; reconcile the provider's actual part state and use an application-owned part plan.

sources.title: Amazon S3: Lifecycle configuration examples
sources.version_or_commit: AWS S3 User Guide, live documentation; page version not stated
sources.locator: Abort incomplete multipart uploads example; AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload action
sources.observed_operation: S3 lifecycle cleanup of incomplete multipart upload parts
sources.claim_scope: A lifecycle rule can abort incomplete MPUs after configured DaysAfterInitiation; documentation gives a seven-day example.
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: Seven days is an example configuration, not a universal AWS default or retention recommendation.
sources.applicability: Use only after owner chooses policy and provider confirms lifecycle support.

sources.title: Amazon S3: Checking object integrity during upload
sources.version_or_commit: AWS S3 User Guide, live documentation; page version not stated
sources.locator: Multipart uploads; full-object checksums; checksum algorithm behavior
sources.observed_operation: Amazon S3 multipart checksum initiation, UploadPart, completion and checksum retrieval
sources.claim_scope: Multipart full-object checksums support CRC64NVME, CRC32, and CRC32C; SHA-256 is composite-only; multipart ETag is not full-object MD5; documented checksum part numbers are consecutive starting at 1.
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: If checksum algorithm is omitted at CreateMultipartUpload, some completion checksum headers can be accepted without being validated or stored. AWS validates and stores a supplied full-object CRC checksum under documented conditions.
sources.applicability: AWS-specific; choose only after the archive provider's end-to-end checksum support and scope are confirmed.

sources.title: Amazon S3 API: CompleteMultipartUpload
sources.version_or_commit: AWS S3 API reference, live documentation; API reference version not stated
sources.claim_scope: A response can begin with HTTP 200 and later contain an embedded Error in the response body; completion can take minutes.
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: AWS SDKs handle this response behavior; a direct REST client must parse the body instead of trusting the initial status alone.
sources.applicability: AWS REST behavior; test the selected provider and SDK/client.

sources.title: Uppy AWS S3 plugin documentation
sources.version_or_commit: Current unversioned documentation; page includes CDN example pinned to Uppy v5.2.1
sources.locator: Multipart uploads; signing; CORS; shouldUseMultipart; headersToExpose
sources.observed_operation: Browser client signing and S3 multipart operations
sources.claim_scope: Docs describe per-operation signing, CORS requirements including exposed ETag and permitted required headers/methods, and a default multipart threshold of 100 MiB.
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: Threshold is Uppy configuration behavior in current unversioned docs; exact plugin release and service compatibility must be pinned and tested. Signing belongs on a server-side endpoint; do not expose long-lived credentials.
sources.applicability: Candidate browser implementation, not an established archive dependency or provider compatibility guarantee.

sources.title: Uppy Golden Retriever documentation
sources.locator: Recovery after browser restart; IndexedDB; service worker behavior
sources.claim_scope: IndexedDB saves file data up to a 10 MiB default; large file references use temporary browser storage and are not reliable across browser crash/restart.
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: Recovery can require the user to reselect the original file. This is a browser persistence behavior, separate from object-store MPU part limits.
sources.applicability: Browser UX/recovery consideration; confirm exact pinned library behavior.

sources.title: tus Resumable Upload Protocol 1.0.0
sources.locator: Core protocol: Upload-Length, HEAD, PATCH, Upload-Offset; checksum, expiration and termination extensions
sources.claim_scope: Client discovers current offset with HEAD and sends PATCH at Upload-Offset; Upload-Length provides known size. Checksum, expiry and termination are optional extensions that servers advertise.
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: Checksum extension verifies individual PATCH body/chunk, not a whole-file digest by itself. Client must honor advertised extensions and current offset.
sources.applicability: Analogous resumable transfer mechanism; does not by itself specify final archival integrity or storage semantics.

sources.title: tusd v2.10.1 S3 storage backend
sources.locator: S3 backend requirements; metadata; temporary part handling; R2-specific part sizing
sources.observed_operation: tusd S3-compatible backend with multipart upload
sources.claim_scope: Backend stores .info metadata, uses S3 multipart upload, and does not expose the final object until completion; PATCH bodies use temporary disk.
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: Requires strong read-after-write consistency; multiple instances need distributed locking. Docs specify R2 equal-sized nonfinal parts and recommend 50 MiB optimal part size for R2. Inspect API logs for incompatible S3 service behavior.
sources.applicability: Server-relay/resumable alternative; additional disk, consistency and locking operations; confirm deployed backend.

sources.title: Amazon S3: Conditional writes
sources.version_or_commit: AWS S3 User Guide, live documentation; page version not stated
sources.locator: If-None-Match and If-Match conditions for PutObject and CompleteMultipartUpload
sources.claim_scope: AWS supports conditional write conditions for PutObject and CompleteMultipartUpload.
sources.conditions_defaults_exceptions: CreateMultipartUpload and UploadPart do not accept the conditions; in-progress MPUs do not count as existing objects; concurrent outcomes include conflict/precondition responses. AWS-specific.
sources.applicability: Supplement application idempotency and unique keys; provider support must be confirmed.
